records.source_rule: A complicated move is not Unnecessary when it provides a side benefit such as picking up an additional useful card, even if the main card could have received a direct Play Clue.
records.learning_objective: Treat a genuine extra useful touch as a side benefit that blocks Unnecessary status.
records.critical_variable: The complicated clue gives positive information to an additional useful card that the direct Play Clue would not touch.
records.blind_answer: Treat the move as Necessary for Level 24 and add no Unnecessary extra effect.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly says picking up an extra useful card is a side benefit.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Add the Unnecessary extra effect merely because a direct clue existed; that ignores the side benefit.
records.mutation: Remove the extra useful touch and, absent another benefit, the move can become Unnecessary.
records.noise: The direct-clue alternative and the second useful card are both needed to test the side-benefit boundary.

records.source_rule: Filling in a previously clued card counts as a side benefit only for positive clues; negative fill-in does not make a move Necessary.
records.learning_objective: Distinguish positive from negative fill-in when deciding whether a move is Unnecessary.
records.critical_variable: Case A adds positive information while case B adds only negative information.
records.blind_answer: Only case A can use fill-in as a side benefit; case B remains Unnecessary absent another benefit.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly counts only positive fill-in as Necessary.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Treat both positive and negative fill-in as side benefits; that erases the source's sign restriction.
records.mutation: Change case B to a positive clue and its fill-in can also block Unnecessary status.
records.noise: The two cases differ only in clue sign so the tested variable is isolated.

records.source_rule: An Unnecessary Trash Chop Move is explicitly illegal because it would be indistinguishable from a Chop Move Ignition.
records.learning_objective: Reject the prohibited Unnecessary Trash Chop Move construction.
records.critical_variable: The Trash Chop Move has no side benefit and would otherwise be classified as Unnecessary.
records.blind_answer: Alice must not deliberately use an Unnecessary Trash Chop Move.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly declares this move illegal rather than assigning it an extra meaning.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Perform the move and ask the team to infer a Level 24 extra effect; it is indistinguishable from Chop Move Ignition.
records.mutation: Give the move a genuine side benefit so it is no longer Unnecessary; the specific prohibition no longer applies on that basis.
records.noise: The available direct Play Clue establishes why the move would otherwise be unnecessary.

records.source_rule: For an Unnecessary move using unknown trash, an off-chop target adds a Chop Move while an on-chop target adds a Trash Push.
records.learning_objective: Switch the extra effect from Chop Move to Trash Push when unknown trash moves onto chop.
records.critical_variable: The same unknown-trash clue target is moved from off chop to on chop.
records.blind_answer: The extra effect becomes a Trash Push.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source partitions unknown-trash effects explicitly by chop position.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Keep the Chop Move interpretation after moving the target onto chop; that uses the wrong branch.
records.mutation: Move the target back off chop and the extra effect returns to Chop Move.
records.noise: All facts except chop position are held constant to isolate the branch condition.

records.source_rule: Unknown trash used off chop by an Unnecessary move produces a Chop Move and can create information asymmetry: the blind-playing player does not know the card is Chop Moved while the other players do until it is demonstrated.
records.learning_objective: Preserve asymmetric knowledge created by the off-chop unknown-trash extra effect.
records.critical_variable: The target was unknown trash off chop and the blind-playing player does not yet know it was trash.
records.blind_answer: Apply a Chop Move and preserve that the blind-playing player initially lacks the Chop Moved information.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source explicitly warns that this branch creates asymmetric knowledge.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Treat all players as immediately knowing the Chop Move; that leaks information to the blind-playing player.
records.mutation: Use known trash instead and the extra effect changes to Ignition rather than this off-chop Chop Move branch.
records.noise: The question states the blind player's knowledge boundary explicitly so the answer cannot rely on hidden shared information.

records.source_rule: If the Chop Move created by an Unnecessary Unknown Trash Discharge would knowingly Chop Move trash, existing Bad Chop Move Ejection logic applies and can continue the interpretation into an Ejection chain.
records.learning_objective: Compose the Level 24 extra Chop Move with the existing Bad Chop Move Ejection protection.
records.critical_variable: Cathy sees that the Level 24 Chop Move would move a card that is already trash.
records.blind_answer: Use the appropriate Bad Chop Move Ejection blind-play instead of allowing the bad Chop Move.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The source example explicitly continues an unnecessary-move interpretation through Bad Chop Move Ejection.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Let Donald knowingly Chop Move trash; that ignores the existing protection rule.
records.mutation: Make Donald's would-be Chop Moved card useful and the Bad Chop Move Ejection trigger disappears.
records.noise: The direct-clue alternative establishes Unnecessary status; the trash identity establishes the Ejection trigger.

records.source_rule: Known trash in an Unnecessary move normally Ignites Bob, but if Bob already has a play and sees playable Finesse Position cards on later players, the Ignition goes to the last player with a visible playable Finesse Position.
records.learning_objective: Apply the first explicit exception to Bob-default Ignition targeting.
records.critical_variable: Bob already has a known play and sees playable Finesse Position cards on Cathy and later Donald.
records.opposite_answer_breaker: The exception sends the Ignition to the last player with the visible playable Finesse Position, not automatically to Bob.
records.actor_direct_alternative: Ignite Bob by the default rule; Bob's existing play and later visible playables activate the exception.
records.mutation: Remove Bob's existing playable card and the default Ignition target returns to Bob.
records.noise: Cathy's playable position is needed to test that the exception chooses the last eligible player, Donald.
